question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x-8y+12z=-8 \\ x-2y+3z=-2 \\ -2x+4y-6z=4\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 12 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -8 & 12 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 4 & -8 & 12 & -8 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -6 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+3z=-2 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations, we can remove these equations from the system. 

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables, $y,$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y$ and $z.$ 

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=2y-3z-2 \\ y=y \\ z=z,\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ and $z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2y-3z-2 \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],\,y,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
